notes: Argaam.com (already GEM's own Status[ref] for this row) independently confirms the GASCO-built 37 km / 12-inch line and states its purpose as delivering gas to 'two sugar and paper factories' and residential Edfu — this corroborates (2nd independent source, alongside Youm7 2022) the prior-suggestion's characterization of Edfu city as the delivery/terminal end. Youm7 (2025) and Elbalad confirm Egypt Gas Company's LOCAL distribution build-out around Edfu/Kom Ombo/Nasr al-Nuba markaz (a different infrastructure layer — low-pressure household/industrial distribution fed off this GASCO transmission spur), which is consistent with, but does not itself pin down, the transmission-line trunk tie-in. I could not find any source (Arabic or English) that names the specific valve-room or km-point where the 37 km line leaves the Dahshour–Aswan ('Upper Egypt') trunk — Kom Ombo is the best-supported bounding candidate (documented pressure-reduction/metering hub in that corridor) but is NOT itself confirmed as the tie-in, and Kom Ombo–Edfu is only ~15–20 km by road versus the sheet's 37 km, so treat 'near Kom Ombo' as a loose bound, not a fix. Recommend leaving this at ROUTE_PARTIAL (corridor-only, no two-point candidate) pending a GASCO network map or tender document naming the tie-in station explicitly. RouteAccuracy should stay capped at 'low' per the source ladder rules.

StartState/Province and EndState/Province are both 'Sinia' — this is a misspelling/transliteration of 'Sinai' (Arabic سيناء), NOT صينية, El-Saff, or Sinnuris. Confirmed independently: GASCO's own EGPC-published progress reports (Petroleum Magazine, Dec-2024 and Nov-2025 issues) describe a project called 'خط إزدواج عبر سيناء' ('Trans-Sinai duplication line'), 36-inch diameter — the Dec-2024 issue states this 15 km segment was completed and gas flow began 2024/6/8, matching P8008 (36in, 15.5km, StartYear1=2024, StartMonth1=6) almost exactly. THIS PIPELINE IS IN/NEAR THE SINAI PENINSULA, NOT UPPER EGYPT — it appears to have been mis-scoped into this 'research_payload_upper_egypt.json' batch. Recommend re-routing to a Sinai/Suez-Canal-region batch.
notes: 'Sinia' resolved: it is GASCO's own transliteration convention for 'Sinai' (compare EndState/Province='Sinia' also used elsewhere in the same GGIT snapshot for the unrelated 'Trans Gulf Gas Pipeline', StartLocation='Petreco Plant' — confirming 'Sinia' is a recurring sheet spelling for the Sinai Peninsula, not a one-off typo). The Arabic project name 'ازدواج سيناء' means 'Sinai duplication/twinning' — i.e. this is additional (looped/parallel) pipe added alongside an existing Trans-Sinai gas transmission corridor for capacity, not a new standalone route. Two candidate PARENT corridors were found (either could be what's being duplicated, or it could be a different unlisted stretch): (1) GASCO's 'El Tina – Abu Sultan Onshore Gas Pipeline' (32-inch, 60 km, built ~2005–06, financed via EIB) — a 2005 Environmental Impact Assessment gives its exact valve-room endpoints: starts at a valve room north of the Al Qantara–Fakous road (32°15'20"E, 30°49'50"N) and ties in at a valve room north of the Abu Sultan–Cairo road (32°09'28"E, 30°23'50"N) — this runs on the WEST bank of the Suez Canal (Ismailia/Sharqia), feeding Abu Sultan and Ataqa power stations and 'supporting the Oyoun Mossa pipeline' (which continues into Sinai proper). (2) The separately-reported 'Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline', El-Tina East to El-Arish, ~111 km, explicitly on the Sinai (east) side and also described as a capacity-duplication project. I could NOT confirm which of these (or which specific km-stretch) the 15.5 km P8008 segment corresponds to, so no defensible two-point endpoint pair could be sourced — marking unresolved rather than guessing. Diameter (36in) and both segments' lengths (15/15.5 km and 28/27 km) match the sheet closely enough to firmly confirm PID identity even without a route. Recommend: (a) re-scope this PID out of the Upper Egypt batch, (b) if pursued, search Egyptian contractor/EPC press releases (Petrojet, Enppi, Orascom Construction) for the specific 'ازدواج عبر سيناء' contract announcement, which sometimes names exact valve-room tie-ins the way the El Tina–Abu Sultan EIA did.
